name: Bhogi & Makar Sankranti
notes: Major Telugu harvest festival celebrated with Bhogi bonfires, colorful Rangoli (Muggulu), kite flying, Haridasu songs, and festive feasts.

name: Kanuma
notes: Third day of Sankranti dedicated to honoring cattle, decorating bulls, and village sports.

name: International Kite & Sweet Festival
notes: Global festival featuring international kite flyers, night kite flying, and traditional sweet stalls at Parade Ground.

name: Nagoba Jatara
notes: Famous Mesram clan Gond tribal festival featuring sacred snake rituals and traditional tribal music and dance.

name: Maha Shivaratri
notes: Major Shiva festival celebrated across all 33 Telangana districts with night-long vigils (Jagaram), fasting, and special Abhishekams.

name: Holy Month of Ramzan & Haleem Season
notes: Month-long sacred fasting period marked by vibrant night shopping bazaars around Charminar, midnight food walks, and world-famous Hyderabadi Haleem stalls.

name: Sammakka Saralamma Medaram Jatara
notes: World's largest biennial tribal congregation, honoring mother-daughter tribal deities with offerings of jaggery (Bangaram).

name: Holi & Kamadahanam
notes: Festival of Colors marking spring arrival, preceded by Kamadahanam bonfires, music, and community celebrations.

name: Ugadi (Telugu New Year)
notes: Telugu New Year celebrated with Ugadi Pachadi (six flavors of life), Panchanga Sravanam, and festive family meals.

name: Eid al-Fitr (Ramzan Eid)
notes: Grand Islamic festival celebrating the culmination of Ramzan fasting, with congregational prayers at Macca Masjid and festive culinary delights (Sheer Khurma).

name: Sri Rama Navami
notes: Celebrates birth of Lord Rama and Sita Ramachandraswamy Kalyanam with royal splendor at Bhadrachalam and local temples.

name: Hanuman Jayanti
notes: Birth celebration of Lord Hanuman, drawing lakhs of devotees wearing Hanuman Diksha robes to Kondagattu and local shrines.

name: Bonalu Festival
notes: Telangana state festival honoring Goddess Mahakali across Golconda, Secunderabad, and Old City with colorful processions (Pothuraju).

name: Varalakshmi Vratam
notes: Sacred auspicious puja performed by married women for well-being, prosperity, and family grace.

name: Vinayaka Chaturthi (Ganesh Chaturthi)
notes: Grand 11-day worship of Lord Ganesha featuring the famous giant Khairatabad idol and massive Hussain Sagar immersion procession.

name: Bathukamma
notes: Telangana floral state festival celebrating nature and Goddess Gauri with unique multi-tiered flower stacks and folk songs.

name: Vijayadasami (Dasara)
notes: Victory of good over evil, celebrated with Jammi tree worship, Alai-Balai greetings, and vehicle pujas.

name: Atla Tadde
notes: Traditional festival celebrated by Telugu women for marital bliss, featuring early morning Atlu (dosas), swings, and moonrise pujas.

name: Deepavali (Diwali) & Kedareswara Vratam
notes: Festival of Lights celebrated with clay lamps (diyas), fireworks, Lakshmi Puja, and Kedareswara Vratam.

name: Nagula Chavithi
notes: Traditional festival dedicated to Serpent God (Naga Devata) worship with milk, eggs, and sesame sweets at ant-hills (Putta).

name: Karthika Purnima & Jwala Toranam
notes: Auspicious full moon night celebrated with deepotsavam (floating oil lamps), temple lighting, and Jwala Toranam bonfires.

name: Subrahmanya Sashti
notes: Festival honoring Lord Subrahmanya (Murugan) with special temple pujas, kavadi offerings, and fasting.

name: Christmas & New Year Celebrations
notes: Winter festive illuminations, midnight church services at St. Mary's Basilica Secunderabad, and citywide New Year events.
